evidence.correctness: Every formula I recomputed against my own code (numpy companion-matrix roots and discrete Lyapunov, a raw-SGD Monte Carlo, the Levin-May 1976 closed form) agreed: the stability limit c_max for tau=1,2,3,5,8,16 (1, 0.618034, 0.445042, 0.28463, 0.184537, 0.095164), the stationary Var x/e2 for c=0.05 and 0.2 at tau=0,1,2,4 (10.256/10.783/11.339/12.552 and 2.778/3.409/4.240/7.226), the double-root radius tau/(tau+1), and the worker noise (MC 0.09874 against the code's 0.098644). The formulas are right. The one rule that fails is the generalisation tau*=ceil(L/Tc), and that counts against claims.
evidence.completeness: README commands ran. `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 11 tests OK in 1.2 s, as stated. `PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py` took 8.3 s, and its output diffs IDENTICAL to experiments/results.txt. Every number in whitepaper sections 1-5 appears in results.txt. The figure script parses results.txt instead of retyping numbers. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: 11 unit tests check the closed forms, the stability crossing, the double root and simulation-vs-formula agreement (5% tolerance). Mutation runs with quality_mutate.py: a wrong c_max argument and a wrong worker-noise exponent were caught. Squaring r in rounds_to_shrink, which halves every round count behind the headline wall-clock speed-ups, SURVIVED. Swapping max for min in alpha_for_floor's s_max survived as well, though that mutant is close to equivalent because unstable steps return inf. Nothing tests rounds_to_shrink or the wall-clock optimisation in section 6.
evidence.craft: Read model.py (161 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py and figure.py. The code is small, clear and dependency-free, with docstrings that state the model. Weak points: there is no input validation (tau<0 or c<=0 is handled only in var_delay); the hand-rolled Durand-Kerner and Gaussian elimination have no convergence check or warning; and simulation results carry no standard error.
evidence.claims: README:3 says the wall-clock-optimal delay is 'exactly ceil(latency/compute time)'. This was tested for only one target floor (F at alpha=0.3). I reran section 6 with the shipped functions at other targets. With F set by alpha0=2.0 and L/Tc=7 the optimum is tau=2 (wall-clock 477), and ceil gives tau=7 (1534, 3.2x slower). At alpha0=3.0 the optimum is tau=0 for every L tested. The whitepaper's limitations line hedges ('observed optimum'), but README and pyproject do not. The whitepaper also presents the stability limit and the double-root rate as its 'Exact results' with no citation, though both are classical (Levin & May 1976; Kuruklis 1994), so novelty is overstated. The claims of 0.3% simulation agreement, the 1%-at-alpha=1e-3 result and the 1.9x-7.5x speed-ups are backed by results.txt for the configuration stated.
evidence.fitness: Research bar (research/CLAUDE.md: PhD level, a programme aimed at a named venue). This is a 24-line note. Its nearest prior work is not cited: Levin & May 1976 and Kuruklis 1994 for x_{t+1}=x_t - c x_{t-tau}; Arjevani, Shamir & Srebro 2020 and Mitliagkas et al. 2016 for delayed SGD on quadratics, where the step scales like 1/tau; Douillard et al. 2023 (DiLoCo); and Douillard et al. 2025 (Streaming DiLoCo) and Kale et al. 2025 (eager updates for overlapped DiLoCo) for the systems it models. The genuinely new piece is the iso-floor wall-clock trade-off, which is a numerical observation on one 3-mode quadratic and one target and does not hold at other targets. A researcher could reuse the verified formulas but not the headline rule.
evidence.domain: A delayed-optimization reviewer would first check whether the dynamics match real overlapped DiLoCo. In Streaming DiLoCo and eager-update schemes, workers keep their local trajectory and merge a delayed outer delta. Here workers restart from a stale global model, which is the classical asynchronous-SGD model. The paper does not discuss that departure. The derivations within the model are correct. There are no confidence intervals or multiple seeds on the simulation ratios (one seed per row), and the rounds-to-converge measure uses only the asymptotic spectral radius.

defects.what: README states the wall-clock-optimal delay is 'exactly ceil(latency / compute time)'. It was observed for one target floor only. At a target set by alpha0=2.0 with L/Tc=7 the shipped functions give tau*=2 (wall-clock 477), while ceil gives tau=7 (1534, 3.2x slower). At alpha0=3.0, tau*=0 for every L.

The stability limit c < 2 sin(pi/(4tau+2)) and the double-root fastest rate are presented as the paper's 'Exact results' with no citation. Both are classical for x_{t+1}=x_t - c x_{t-tau} (Levin & May 1976; Kuruklis 1994). Delayed SGD on quadratics (Arjevani, Shamir & Srebro 2020; Mitliagkas et al. 2016), DiLoCo (Douillard et al. 2023), Streaming DiLoCo (Douillard et al. 2025) and eager updates (Kale et al. 2025) are also uncited, so novelty is overstated.
The tau*=ceil(L/Tc) rule is generalised from a single target floor F (tau=0 at alpha=0.3) on one 3-mode quadratic. The grid never varies F, and at larger targets the rule fails.
rounds_to_shrink and the section-6 wall-clock optimisation behind the headline 1.9x-7.5x speed-ups are untested: squaring r (halving every round count) leaves all 11 tests green.

Workers restart from the stale global model (the classical async-SGD model). Real overlapped DiLoCo (Streaming DiLoCo, eager updates) has workers continue locally and merge a delayed outer delta. The departure is neither modelled nor listed in the limitations.
Simulation-vs-exact ratios are single-seed with no standard error or CI. The test tolerance is 5%, while the README claims 0.3%.

verdict: The formulas are correct. I recomputed the stability limit, the stationary variance, the double-root rate and the worker noise against numpy companion-matrix roots, a discrete Lyapunov solve, a raw-SGD Monte Carlo and the Levin-May closed form, and all agreed. The experiments rerun byte-identical in 8 s. The work still does not meet the research bar. The README headline 'optimal delay is exactly ceil(L/Tc)' fails as soon as the target floor changes (alpha0=2, L/Tc=7: tau*=2, and ceil is 3.2x slower). The 'exact results' are classical delay-difference facts (Levin & May 1976) presented without citation, next to an uncited delayed-SGD and Streaming-DiLoCo literature. The wall-clock path the speed-ups rest on is untested (a halving mutant survived). And the stale-restart model departs from how overlapped DiLoCo actually works. It is a correct 24-line note, not a publishable contribution.
